answer:
The documents don't state a maximum number of dimensions for a "bitvec" type. pgvector's type is called `bit`, and the retrieved text only gives its storage size: "Each bit vector takes `dimensions / 8 + 8` bytes of storage." [pgvector/README.md]

The nearest related limit is for indexing, not for the type itself: "You can use [half-precision vectors](#half-precision-vectors) or [half-precision indexing](#half-precision-indexing) to index up to 4,000 dimensions or [binary quantization](#binary-quantization) to index up to 64,000 dimensions." [pgvector/README.md]

So binary quantization can index up to 64,000 dimensions, but I don't know the maximum dimensions the `bit` type can hold. The only per-type limit stated is for `vector`: "Vectors can have up to 16,000 dimensions." [pgvector/README.md]
